requirement: One real-world horse should converge to one durable canonical identity within the Founder-approved identity-scope model.
The horse subject must remain representable without an account, facility, organization, invoice, provider, or public profile.
Canonical Horse ID must remain stable through changes in name, relationship, facility, trainer, rider, provider, account, location, work, retirement, death, and archive.
A canonical Horse ID must not be presented as legal title or registry title.
Planned, expected, pregnancy-loss, stillbirth, live-born, first-known, deceased, and erroneous existence states must remain distinct.
A planned or expected foal must not silently become an active live-horse identity.
A live-born or first-known horse identity must be independently durable and linked to predecessor planning or intake records.
The system must support exact, partial, approximate, conflicting, and unknown identity facts.
Every material horse fact must identify source, owner, version, effective time, verification state, confidence basis, and correction state.
Imported data must remain a claim until governed reconciliation establishes its status.
Estimated or asserted values must not display as verified exact facts.
Current truth, historical snapshots, source-owned references, and derived projections must remain distinguishable.
A copied label or cached value must not become editable canonical truth.
Conflicting material facts must be surfaced and must not use blind last-write-wins.
Correction must preserve the original record and create an attributable successor.
Historical decisions and exports must retain the exact fact versions they used.
Identity disputes must route to Claims and Evidence governance.
Configuration changes must not retroactively reinterpret historical horse facts without controlled reconciliation.
Horse Profile must be a bounded projection rather than the canonical record.
Horse Passport must be purpose-specific, permission-filtered, source-versioned, and time-stamped.
Passport must state omissions, limitations, expiry where applicable, and that it is not title or completeness proof.
Passport omission must not delete the underlying source record.
Profile, Passport, search, report, export, public, provider, emergency, and memorial projections must be separately governed.
Projection generation must record policy version, source versions, permission watermark, purpose, and requesting actor.
Stale projections must be expired, revoked, or regenerated when material watermarks change.
Public and marketplace projections must be private or off by default unless separately authorized.
Search must support current and former names without exposing restricted raw identifiers.
Reports must identify definition owner, population, time period, completeness, exclusions, and correction status.
Horse lifecycle must use multiple axes rather than one global status field.
Compatible time-bounded lifecycle statuses may coexist.
Lifecycle compatibility and precedence rules must be versioned and historically stable.
Current operational state must not erase historical state.
Retirement must adapt operations without hiding the horse.
Missing, stolen, seized, impounded, disputed, and unknown-location states must support heightened restrictions.
Eligibility facts must identify requirement source, status, evidence, effective time, expiry, and dispute state.
Eligibility workflow results must not rewrite canonical horse facts.
Item 04 eligibility facts must remain distinct from Item 08 workflow, Item 06 timing, and Item 09 financial consequences.
Reproductive and pedigree relationships must distinguish genetic, gestational, registry, ownership, and service roles.
Foal identity must be linked to, not collapsed into, parent or recipient-mare records.
Duplicate candidates must be investigated before destructive convergence.
No duplicate decision may rely solely on name, color, breed, owner, facility, photo similarity, or vendor ID.
Merge must require explicit authority, multi-source evidence, conflict review, and full lineage preservation.
Merge must preserve candidate IDs, source records, restrictions, disputes, and prior decisions.
Merge must not grant new permission.
Unmerge and split correction must be supported through governed reconciliation.
Every downstream horse reference must reconcile after merge, unmerge, or split correction.
Duplicate and merge decisions must be reversible without deleting evidence.
AI or probabilistic matching may propose but may not decide merge.
Vendor deletion must not delete canonical horse identity or history.
Transfer must be a governed state machine rather than an owner-field edit.
Transfer must preserve canonical Horse ID.
Transfer must identify parties, authority, evidence, restrictions, disputes, and purpose-specific effective times.
Transfer must prepare a permission-filtered continuity packet.
Transfer must establish successor access and remove obsolete access through Item 03.
Transfer completion must be blocked while critical identity, access, care-continuity, evidence, or required notice obligations remain unresolved.
Former parties must retain only purpose-specific history permitted by current governance.
Payment, possession, facility presence, authorship, or prior relationship must not create ownership or continuing authority.
Custody, possession, ownership, lease, care, payment, facility, and stewardship must remain distinct.
Current location, home facility, temporary location, transport, hospital, quarantine, evacuation, and historical location must remain distinct.
Location references must point to Item 02 topology rather than duplicate it.
Precise location must support suppression or generalization for security, theft, dispute, safeguarding, and emergency risk.
Movement episodes must preserve origin, destination, responsible party, timing, handoff, condition, documents, and exceptions as applicable.
Death must not delete identity, history, evidence, or permitted memories.
Cause of death, euthanasia, remains, necropsy, insurance, and memorial content must be separately sensitivity-controlled.
Public memorialization must be voluntary where required and permission-filtered.
Archive must prevent ordinary mutation while allowing authorized correction, claims, legal holds, retention actions, and memorial management.
Erroneous death, archive, activation, merge, or identity state must be corrected through attributable successor events.
Account closure, facility closure, relationship end, or vendor removal must not delete horse continuity.
All access to horse data must use Item 03 permission and field-level projection.
Wrong-horse and wrong-tenant requests must fail closed without enumeration.
Sensitive location, dispute, reproductive, health-context, death, insurance, and protected-participant data must receive heightened controls.
Support access must be ticketed, purpose-bound, time-limited, attributable, revocable, and reviewable.
Exports must be purpose-bound, minimized, watermarked, attributable, and auditable.
Horse data must not create opaque value, danger, quality, suitability, lameness, welfare, temperament, insurability, or performance scores.
Public search must prevent enumeration by restricted identifier or precise location.
Media and extracted metadata must remain evidence claims rather than conclusive identity, medical, behavior, or ownership proof.
Offline work may preserve only non-authoritative proposals for permitted low-risk observations or evidence capture.
Offline operation must not finalize identity activation, merge, unmerge, split correction, transfer, death, archive, memorial, permission, or unrestricted Passport.
Synchronization must reauthenticate, reauthorize, recheck duplicate state, compare versions, and detect wrong-horse, wrong-tenant, stale, replayed, or restriction-conflicting proposals.
Offline queue state must remain visible and materially conflicting changes must not use last-write-wins.
AI may summarize cited evidence, identify gaps, compare claims, and draft proposals.
AI may not make final identity, merge, ownership, custody, medical, welfare, legal, transfer, publication, or permission decisions.
Automation must use a named system actor, accountable human, narrow purpose, exact versions, evidence, idempotency, monitoring, and escalation.
External integrations must be typed, versioned, tenant-scoped, idempotent, and non-authority-creating.
External data retraction must preserve prior source history and correction lineage.
Analytics must disclose context, missingness, uncertainty, and definition ownership.
Every consequential event must identify canonical and candidate IDs, actor, authority, source, policy, configuration, time, correlation, and reconciliation status.
Future implementation must be deterministic, non-destructive, tenant-isolated, explainable, auditable, source-aware, accessible, and resilient.
Future implementation must prove referential integrity and no orphaned downstream references after convergence corrections.
Migration must preserve legacy IDs, provenance, approximate dates, disputes, restrictions, and source systems.
Migration must quarantine ambiguity and prohibit automatic merge or authority manufacture.
Rollback must preserve horse identity, history, evidence, transfer state, convergence lineage, and corrections.
Operational targets, runbooks, alerts, staffing, recovery proof, and support readiness must be approved before production.
All 43 canonical sections must remain present and in order.
The five readiness questions must use exact active wording and permitted answer vocabulary.
Questions 1 through 3 must be YES_WITH_EVIDENCE before implementation authorization.
All five questions must be YES_WITH_EVIDENCE before first-user enrollment.
Every unresolved Founder decision must identify recommendation, rationale, source, affected requirements, and gate effect.
Independent review, approval, adoption, implementation, release, and enrollment must remain separately represented.
This candidate must not authorize schema, migration, deployment, production, external activation, public launch, or enrollment.
Horse identity scope across tenants must be explicit, versioned, and Founder-approved before implementation.
Cross-tenant matching must not disclose another tenant, horse-record existence, canonical internal ID, or protected content without authority.
Cross-tenant identity and transfer matching must use blind or mediated workflows with attributable evidence and audit.
Canonical internal Horse IDs must not be public or enumerable locators; shared surfaces must use public-safe references.
External identifiers must be qualified by issuer, namespace, jurisdiction, type, and effective period before uniqueness or match decisions.
Replaced, duplicated, mistyped, fraudulent, retracted, or disputed identifiers must preserve prior claims and correction lineage.
Horse age must be derived from source-qualified birth evidence and an explicit as-of date rather than stored as stale canonical truth.
Twins, clones, and genetically identical horses must retain separate canonical identities; DNA or pedigree alone must not authorize merge.
Reproductive predecessor records must support zero, one, or multiple outcomes, with a separate Horse ID for every live-born horse.
Every continuity packet must identify omissions, conflicts, stale sources, restricted items, and completeness limitations.
Transfer must preserve impact-specific effective times for relationship, custody, possession, access, care responsibility, facility assignment, financial context, and other governed consequences.
Transfer approval, each impact's effect, downstream reconciliation, and case completion must remain separate states.
Revoking or invalidating a Passport or export must block future trusted reliance but must not be represented as remote deletion of external copies.
Passport and export verification must return minimum safe validity metadata without expanding access to protected horse data.

Human personal data embedded in horse history must remain separately governed and capable of lawful minimization, restriction, correction, pseudonymization, or erasure without deleting horse continuity.
Public, shared, transfer, memorial, and broad projections must control EXIF, precise location, hidden document properties, embedded personal data, and unredacted sensitive metadata.
Death, missing, stolen, recovery, and archive states must trigger permission-filtered downstream reconciliation rather than directly mutating another PIA's truth.
Public missing or stolen alerts must require separate authority, minimum content, expiry, and suppression of owner, minor, and precise-location data.
Merge, unmerge, and split correction must preserve durable, permission-checked tombstones or redirects and prevent broken downstream references.
Horse identity must support unknown, absent, disputed, or changing ownership without forcing or manufacturing an Item 03 relationship.
